title: Tenant cordon thermostat and burst escrow playbook for noisy-neighbor events
creator: Aisha Mukherjee
description: Summary: After the capacity incident on 2026-02-24 where a single tenant's workload caused repeated eviction storms on a tier-2 dedicated cluster, the on-call runbook mitigations (short-term eviction and static throttles) prevented immediate customer-visible errors but revealed gaps in our reservation sizing and burst controls. This ticket collects follow-ups: define a tenant cordon mechanism, implement a reservation thermostat (gradual, telemetry-driven reservation decay/growth), and introduce a burst-escrow allocation to prevent uncontrolled token-burst drain. Goal: reduce eviction frequency by 90% for similar traffic patterns and ensure controlled, observable degradation without hard ejection for first offenders.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Decided to prefer soft cordon (no hard tenant ejection) for first two violations; only hard eject on repeat rapid infra-impacting violations.
2026-03-03: Chose a telemetry-led thermostat model over immediate static caps; thermostat will use 1m, 5m, 30m q95 latency and reservation deficit as inputs.
2026-03-05: Burst escrow implemented as a separate token pool per-tenant that replenishes slowly; escrow tokens burned before touching reservation to preserve steady-state throughput.
action_items: A1: Implement tenant cordon API and coordinator signals (owner: Luis Romero, due: 2026-03-14) - endpoint: POST /internal/tenants/{id}/cordon
A2: Build reservation thermostat prototype in allocator that decays reservation by 5-20% based on deficit trend windows (owner: Priya Anand, due: 2026-03-18)
A3: Add burst-escrow pool with leak-rate limiter and token accounting; safe defaults: escrow=10% of reservation, refill=1%/min (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-03-21)
A4: Extend telemetry to surface escrow burn rate, thermostat actions, and cordon events in Console (owner: Ana Patel, due: 2026-03-17)
A5: Create automated remediation playbook (runbook) that ties Alert->Cordon->Mitigation->Escalation steps and publish to Confluence (owner: Luis Romero, due: 2026-03-16)
A6: Launch synthetic load job to validate thermostat and escrow across representative models (owner: SRE team, ticket: ENG-421999, due: 2026-03-19)
A7: Post-deploy evaluation: collect 2 weeks of telemetry, run automated fairness checks, adjust hysteresis and safety multipliers (owner: Research/Applied ML, due: 2026-04-04)
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha M: Initial incident triage notes attached. Observed long-tail KV cache growth and large prefix churn from tenant T-451 leading to amplified batching and memory pressure.
2026-03-03 - Luis R: Prototype of cordon API submitted as design doc. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DC/Tenant+Cordon+Design

2026-03-04 - Marco C: Burst-escrow design drafted. Key idea: escrow is separate from reservation and cannot be used to bump up reservation; when escrow is exhausted, burst requests are queued or degraded.
2026-03-06 - Priya A: Thermostat algorithm sketch: uses exponential moving average of reservation deficit with safety multiplier 1.25 and minimum hysteresis window 10m to avoid oscillation.
2026-03-08 - Ana P: Added Console mockups showing escrow burn-rate and thermostat events; linked prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/escrow/tenant-burst
2026-03-09 - SRE: Ran preliminary synthetic load; thermostat reduced eviction count by ~67% in early tests. More varied traffic tests scheduled.
2026-03-10 - Product: PM reviewed playbook; asked for clear customer communication templates if we cordon a paying tenant. Added action to draft messaging.
notes: Telemetry schema additions: escrow_burn_rate (tokens/s), thermostat_adjustment_percent, cordon_state (soft|hard), last_cordon_time. We need migrations on allocator config (schema v3). Plan rollback: disable thermostat and revert to reserved static limits. Ensure canary rollout to 5% of clusters before broader rollout.
